fix.item: Added a "Presets" section to README.md, per a Grok review suggestion (scoped down from a full export/import feature, which would need a custom admin controller a system plugin doesn't have): three field-value combinations to copy into the settings screen by hand, Minimal (a small site, nothing extra), Full (every feature on), and Performance (a content-heavy site prioritizing page weight, e.g. "Load only on com_content pages" on, legacy CSS and the DOM-watching MutationObserver off). Documentation only, no code changes.
Every field name referenced was cross-checked against the actual English label strings in the manifest/language file, so an admin can find each one by its exact on-screen name.

Added a rwdTables:enhanced custom event, per a Grok review suggestion, for integrating with other scripts: document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('rwdTables:enhanced', { detail: { table } })) fires once per table, right after every other step of that table's processing, labels, ARIA roles, wrap, min-width, the resize observer, is already done, so a listener always sees a fully-enhanced table, never a half-finished one. Naturally fires only once per table thanks to the existing data-rwd-ready guard: a repeated enhance()/window.rwdTablesEnhance() call (including via the opt-in MutationObserver) is a no-op for tables already processed, so listeners don't need their own deduplication.

Verified via headless render: the event fires exactly once per table on initial load with detail.table.getAttribute('data-rwd-ready') already "1" and the wrap already in place at the moment the listener runs; a repeated manual window.rwdTablesEnhance() call does not re-fire it for those same tables; and a genuinely new table added afterward does fire it, exactly once, fully processed.

Added as permanent Playwright regression tests (not just a one-off manual check) covering both the no-re-fire and fires-once-for-new-table cases. All 31 prior functional assertions re-verified unaffected.

Added a rwd-scroll-only opt-in class, per a Grok review suggestion: a comparison matrix (many columns, where a row only makes sense read across all of them together) loses that grid relationship when turned into a stacked label:value card list. table class="responsiv rwd-scroll-only" never stacks into cards regardless of width, stays a real table and scrolls horizontally instead. Per-table rather than a global setting, so a site can mix ordinary stacking price tables with scroll-only comparison matrices on the same page.

Implementation: observeWidth()'s apply() now checks for the class and forces isStacked = false unconditionally when present (skipping the breakpoint comparison entirely); a small CSS rule sets white-space: nowrap on the table's cells so the browser's own layout can't squeeze columns to fit, giving the table a genuine natural width to overflow, the same "let it overflow and scroll" principle as the --rwd-min-width setting, just scoped to one table. The existing scroll-shadow/tabindex/role="region" logic needed no changes at all: it's already driven by measured overflow (scrollWidth > clientWidth), not by why a table happens to be wide, so a scroll-only table that overflows gets the same accessible scroll region "for free."

Verified via headless render: a 6-column matrix at 320px viewport never gets .is-stacked, genuinely overflows (178px), and picks up tabindex="0"/role="region" automatically; an ordinary table on the same page (no class) still stacks normally, confirming the behaviour is per-table, not global. Added as a permanent Playwright regression fixture (tests/fixtures/scroll-only.html) with two tests. All 31 prior functional assertions re-verified unaffected.

Added dir="rtl" support for the grid layout and generated label, per a Grok review suggestion: replaced four hardcoded physical text-align: left/right declarations (desktop th/td, caption, the tbody/tfoot th[scope=row] block treatment, and the mobile card's .rwd-value) with their logical equivalents (start/end). CSS Grid's own track placement already follows the inline direction on its own, it needed no changes, but was previously undermined by the physical text-align: right on .rwd-value, which would have kept the value hugging the visual right edge even after the grid itself mirrored under RTL.

Verified via headless render, comparing the identical markup under dir="ltr" vs dir="rtl": in LTR the mobile card's value sits near the cell's right edge; in RTL it sits near the left edge, a genuine mirror, not just a text-align change, confirmed by measuring actual pixel positions rather than trusting the CSS spec's stated behavior alone. Desktop header text-align computes to start under RTL (resolves to the correct visual side) instead of a hardcoded left.

Documented a real, out-of-scope limitation: the scroll-shadow indicator (can-scroll-left/can-scroll-right, driven by JS reading scrollLeft) is not RTL-aware, since browsers measure horizontal scroll position differently under RTL. Only affects the narrow combination of an RTL page AND the opt-in min-width horizontal-scroll setting, a stacked card or a table that fits without scrolling (the common RTL case) is unaffected.

Added a permanent Playwright regression fixture (tests/fixtures/rtl.html) and two tests covering both the desktop header and the stacked card's mirrored grid, so this can't silently regress later. All 31 existing functional assertions re-verified unaffected (LTR, the default, is untouched).

Switched the scrollable region's accessible name from aria-label (a copied, flattened snapshot of the caption's text) to aria-labelledby pointing at the caption element's own id, per a Grok review suggestion, a live reference survives any formatting inside the caption and stays in sync if it ever changes, instead of a one-time text copy. An id is generated only if the caption doesn't already have one (an existing author- or script-supplied id is never overwritten). Falls back to aria-label with the translated scrollLabel string exactly as before when the table has no caption at all.

Verified via headless render across three cases: a caption with no id (one is generated, aria-labelledby correctly points to it), a caption with a pre-existing id (kept untouched, aria-labelledby points to that), and no caption (falls back to aria-label, no aria-labelledby), in every case where aria-labelledby is set, it resolves to a real element in the document.

Added this as a permanent Playwright regression test (tests/fixtures/min-width.html now has a second, captioned scrollable table) rather than a one-off manual check, so this can't silently regress later.

Added a new "Appearance" fieldset with six admin fields (border color, text color, header background color, label text color, card corner radius, card shadow), per a Grok review suggestion, so a quick branding tweak doesn't need a custom.css edit. Each field maps to one of the plugin's CSS custom properties; when at least one is set, onBeforeCompileHead() builds a small inline :root{...} declaration via addStyleDeclaration() and outputs only that, an empty field is skipped entirely, so leaving everything blank (the default) adds no style tag at all and changes nothing.

Deliberately scoped to six fields, not all thirteen CSS variables the plugin defines: found and dropped --rwd-accent-soft from the original plan after checking actual CSS usage, it's defined for both light and dark palettes but never actually consumed by any rule (dead), so exposing an admin field for it would have let someone set a color and see nothing change. Replaced it with --rwd-label (the bold label text color, genuinely used in header cells and each mobile card's field labels) instead. Covers the default (light) palette only, doubling every field for a dark-mode variant would make this settings screen unwieldy for what's meant to be a quick branding tool, not a full theme editor; dark-mode-specific colors still need custom.css.

Defense in depth on the generated CSS: {, }, , and are stripped from each value before use, so a broken or adversarial admin input can't close the style tag early or inject markup, verified with a Python port of the exact PHP logic against a payload containing } /stylescriptalert(1)/scriptstyle, confirming no / survive in the output.

Verified via headless render that setting all six fields actually changes the rendered table: text color, card corner radius, and card box-shadow all matched the configured values exactly. All 31 functional regression assertions re-verified unaffected (nothing is set by default, so existing fixtures are untouched).

Translated the eight new strings (fieldset label + 6 field label/description pairs) into all five supported languages, key parity re-verified (51 keys in every non-English file, none missing or extra).

Added an opt-in "Compose multi-level labels" setting, per a Grok review suggestion: for a grouped header (e.g. "Cena" split into "hodina"/"km"), the mobile card's label was always just the leaf column name ("hodina"), losing which group it belonged to. When enabled, headerLabels() composes the full path through every header row a column passes through instead ("Cena › hodina"), joined by a configurable separator (default " › "). Off by default, matching the existing leaf-only behaviour exactly.

Implementation tracks each spanned column's header text once per originating cell (not once per rowspan-duplicated row) during the same grid-building pass headerLabels() already did, so a column under a single, ungrouped header row is completely unaffected either way (its "path" is just one segment).

Verified via headless render on the same colspan/rowspan grouped-header table used for the v1.7.0 regression test: with the setting on, the body row's cells report data-label="Cena › hodina" / "Cena › km" (and "Stroj", spanned via rowspan, a single origin cell, stays as plain "Stroj", not duplicated); with it off (default), labels are unchanged from before ("hodina"/"km"). All 31 functional regression assertions re-verified unaffected.
Translated the two new setting strings into all five supported languages (en-GB, sk-SK, de-DE, cs-CZ, pl-PL), key parity re-verified (38 keys in every non-English file, none missing or extra).

Added three more languages, per a Grok review suggestion aimed at the wider regional Joomla community: de-DE, cs-CZ, and pl-PL, alongside the existing en-GB and sk-SK. Full translation of every admin-form label/description (34 strings) plus the site-facing .sys.ini description shown on the Discover/Install screen, registered in the manifest's languages block.

Verified all four non-English language files have exactly the same 34+2 keys as en-GB (no missing or extra strings) and that every value is a well-formed KEY="value" line with no unescaped internal quotes that would break Joomla's .ini parser.

Added minified CSS/JS to the release build, per a Grok review suggestion: scripts/minify.sh (terser for JS, clean-css for CSS) generates fgresponsivetables.min.js and *.min.css, each with a source map, run automatically by the release workflow before packaging. No changes to joomla.asset.json or the PHP were needed, confirmed against Joomla's own documentation that the Web Asset Manager automatically prefers a .min. file over its unminified counterpart in the same folder, falling back to the unminified version when Joomla Debug mode is on.

Minified output verified functionally identical to source, not just "minified without error": all 31 functional regression assertions from the Playwright suite re-run against the actual minified files (source-swapped into the same fixtures) and passed. Real measured size reduction: JS 22.8KB → 6.7KB, main CSS 16.8KB → 6.4KB, legacy CSS 2.0KB → 0.85KB.
Minified files and source maps are build output (regenerated fresh on every release), not committed to the repo, added to .gitignore.

Added debouncing (50ms) to the opt-in "Watch for dynamically added tables" MutationObserver, per a Grok review suggestion: a page builder or framework inserting a lot of content at once fires many mutation records in quick succession, and without debouncing each one independently scheduled its own enhance() call. Now a burst of activity collapses into a single call once things settle, instead of one per mutation.

Verified with an A/B test on the same scenario (8 tables inserted 10ms apart, well within the debounce window): 15 enhance() calls without debouncing vs. 4 with it, on identical input, a real, measured reduction, not just a theoretical one. All 8 tables still end up fully processed either way.

Fixed five smaller findings from a P3 review pass: a Czech-ism typo in the Slovak "Load legacy compatible styles" description (úplně → úplne); renamed the script Web Asset from plg_system_fgresponsivetables.tables to .tables-script (was legal since Joomla indexes by type+name, but matched core convention less than a distinct name); added declare(strict_types=1) to Fgresponsivetables.php (free, since every method already has a return type); documented .responsiv-fixed (table-layout: fixed) and .rwd-nowrap in README.md (README.txt already had the latter); made the autoClass container selector list configurable (auto_class_selector, shown only when "Enhance all article tables" is on) instead of hardcoded to Joomla core com_content markup, since templates like Helix, JD, or T4 wrap content differently.

All 31 functional regression assertions re-verified unaffected by these changes; the new auto_class_selector setting itself verified via headless render (a table inside a non-default container class gets .responsiv added when a matching custom selector is configured).

Added a committed Playwright visual/functional regression suite (tests/), addressing a real gap from a P3 finding in the same external analysis: this project has already had one real visual regression ship (the float→flex mobile-card attempt in v1.3.4, reverted in v1.3.5) and multiple bugs an external review found by hand that this kind of suite would have caught automatically. tests/fixtures/*.html load the plugin's real CSS/JS directly (no Joomla involved) with 17 representative tables across 5 fixture pages, covering every P1 bug from the same analysis (colspan/rowspan header resolution, nested tables, rowspan-in-body label shift, th[scope=row] in stacked mode) plus the long-value-overflow fix, shared .table-wrapper handling, min-width scroll behavior, dark mode, and the "lines" card style.

tests/visual.spec.js has two layers: deterministic functional assertions (computed styles, ARIA roles, data-label values, overflow measurements, the actual regression net, no baseline image needed) and screenshots at 320/360/600/768/1200px saved as CI artifacts for human review (not yet diffed against a baseline, tests/README.md explains how to turn this into true pixel-diff testing once a human approves a first "known good" set).
Added .github/workflows/tests.yml, running the suite on every push/PR to master and uploading screenshots + the HTML report as artifacts.

All 31 functional assertions verified directly against the real fixture files and plugin code before committing this (via the headless Chrome available in this environment, translating each Playwright assertion 1:1), genuine confidence this actually works, not just "looks right" syntactically. The Playwright-specific test runner itself hasn't been executed (not available in this environment), so the very first npm test / CI run is the real first end-to-end confirmation of the Playwright config and syntax specifically.

Fixed the release workflow itself, found live on the first real tag push: ./build-check.sh failed with "Permission denied" (exit code 126) because the executable bit wasn't preserved when the repository was committed from Windows. The v2.0.25 tag exists and its code is correct, but the workflow failed before reaching the "create GitHub Release" step, so that release still needs to be finished by hand once, the same way every prior release was.

build-check.sh is now invoked as bash build-check.sh in the workflow, which doesn't depend on the executable bit at all, plus an explicit chmod +x step right after checkout as a second layer of defense (also keeps direct ./build-check.sh invocation working for anyone running it locally after a fresh checkout).
Not yet confirmed on real GitHub Actions infrastructure past this specific failure point, this tag push is the actual first end-to-end test.

Added a GitHub Actions release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml), addressing a real recurring risk from a P3 finding in the same external analysis: version lives in three files (fgresponsivetables.xml, media/joomla.asset.json, updates.xml), and media/joomla.asset.json's version specifically drives cache-busting, so a forgotten bump there means visitors silently keep getting stale CSS/JS from cache even though the manifest says otherwise. From now on, cutting a release means: add the version's entry to the top of CHANGELOG.md, push to master, then tag and push vX.Y.Z. The workflow bumps all three version files, regenerates changelog.xml, verifies all four agree and that the XML/JSON/JS are syntactically valid, packages the ZIP, commits the regenerated files back, and creates the GitHub Release with the ZIP attached.
The workflow fails on purpose if CHANGELOG.md's newest entry doesn't match the tag being pushed, so the exact "forgot to update it somewhere" class of bug this feature targets can't ship silently.

Extracted the changelog.xml generation logic (used by hand for 2.0.18-2.0.24) into scripts/build_changelog_xml.py, and added scripts/set_version.py for the three-file version bump, both reusable manually and by the workflow.

Found and fixed an unrelated bug in the process: .gitignore had build-check.sh listed since the very first commit, meaning it was likely never actually pushed to the repository at all (git silently skips ignored files even under git add .), the ZIP-exclusion and the git-tracking concerns had been conflated; build-check.sh needs to be tracked in git for the new workflow to run it, only the release ZIP itself should exclude it (already handled separately by the packaging step's own exclude list).

Verified locally end to end (not on real GitHub Actions infrastructure, which isn't available in this environment): simulated every step of the workflow in sequence on a scratch copy of the repo, including the "forgot to update CHANGELOG.md" failure case (confirmed it correctly aborts with a clear error instead of shipping a mismatched version), and confirmed scripts/ and .github/ are excluded from the packaged ZIP. Not yet run on real GitHub Actions, please verify the first live tag push carefully.

Fixed one more split point in the changelog display, found live: Joomla's changelog viewer breaks a single item into separate bullets at em/en dashes too, not just ampersands. changelog.xml's generator now replaces every em dash and en dash with a comma across all entries.

Fixed the changelog display for real this time, confirmed broken live again by 2.0.22's own fix: my 2.0.22 changelog entry described the escaping syntax literally (spelling out the entity codes as prose using the ampersand character itself), and that one character hit the exact same underlying problem the entry was describing, Joomla's changelog viewer doesn't re-escape item text before handing it to the browser, so any ampersand in the content gets interpreted as the start of an HTML entity, and the bullet shredded into fragments around each one, same as the tag-name bug did before it.

changelog.xml's generator now also replaces every literal ampersand character in the source text with the word "and" (in addition to stripping angle-bracket tag references), so no ampersand of any kind, entity-shaped or not, ever reaches the output. The 2.0.22 entry above was also rewritten to stop describing the escaping syntax using the character itself, since that's what triggered this in the first place.
Not yet re-confirmed live.

Fixed the changelog display itself, confirmed broken live (no PHP errors this time, the modal opened, but content was shredded into meaningless one-word bullets). Cause: several CHANGELOG.md bullets reference literal HTML/XML tag names in backticks (changelogurl, fix, etc.); these were correctly escaped for the XML file, but Joomla's changelog viewer decodes that escaping back to real angle brackets before displaying, and the browser then parses the tag names as actual (unknown) HTML elements, splitting the bullet into fragments around them instead of showing it as one line.

changelog.xml's generator now strips any bracketed tag reference down to its bare inner text before escaping (a backtick-quoted changelogurl tag name becomes just the word changelogurl), so no tag-like angle-bracket pairs remain in the output at all. A few standalone greater-than signs remain from code snippets (CSS child selectors, a PHP method call), those are safe on their own, since one alone with nothing matching it before doesn't start a tag.
Not yet re-confirmed live for actual readability (only the "no more shredded bullets" fix is new here), please check once more.

Re-added changelogurl/changelog.xml (removed in 2.0.20) with the actually-correct schema this time, verified against Joomla's own documentation (manual.joomla.org): each changelog entry needs element/type/version, then category tags in the SINGULAR, fix, addition, change, remove, security, language, note, each containing plain item children, no title attribute. What 2.0.18/2.0.19 actually shipped (fixesfix title="...", name, description) doesn't match this schema at all, which is exactly why Joomla's Changelog class treated those as undeclared dynamic properties, not a Joomla core bug as 2.0.20 concluded, a wrong schema on our side. All bullets now map to fixitem entries.
Not yet re-confirmed live, the first two attempts both looked correct locally and both failed on the real site, so this needs an actual test on mechanizmysevcik.sk again before being trusted.

Reverted changelogurl and changelog.xml (added in 2.0.18, trimmed further in 2.0.19), confirmed live, on the real production site, that this is genuinely broken, not just noisy: Joomla's Joomla\CMS\Changelog\Changelog class sets every field it parses from the XML, even the most minimal set (name/description/fixes), already trimmed once in 2.0.19 to try to avoid this, as an undeclared dynamic property, which PHP 8.2 deprecates. On this site, no changelog rendered at all, only the PHP deprecation warnings; not a cosmetic log entry, an actually-broken feature.

This is a documented upstream Joomla bug (joomla/joomla-cms#41635), not something our XML content can work around, the same failure mode was already reported there for the most basic possible fields. Tracked as a blocked item in ROADMAP.md to revisit once it's fixed in Joomla core, rather than left half-working in the meantime.

Fixed PHP 8.2+ deprecation warnings reported live on the changelog display (Joomla's own Changelog.php class, tracked upstream as joomla-cms#41635): maintainer, maintainerurl, targetplatformversion, targetplatformname, and client inside a changelog entry aren't declared properties on that class, so Joomla was setting them as dynamic properties, deprecated since PHP 8.2. Those five elements weren't part of the actual changelog schema (I'd added them based on the update schema in updates.xml, which does support them, without verifying the changelog entry schema is different); removed them. changelog.xml entries now only use version, name, description, and fixes/fix, which don't trigger the warning.

Added changelogurl to the manifest and to updates.xml, pointing at a new changelog.xml (Joomla's own changelog XML format) hosted at the repo root, Joomla's Extensions Manager can now show the changelog directly in the update screen instead of sending someone to GitHub. changelog.xml is generated from CHANGELOG.md itself (one changelog entry per version, each bullet as a fix), so it stays in sync with the same source of truth rather than being maintained twice by hand.
build-check.sh now also checks changelog.xml's newest entry against the other three version sources before allowing a package/tag.

Documented a known trade-off (bod 16 from the same external analysis): the mobile card's content: attr(data-label) generated-content label can be read twice by some screen readers (VoiceOver, NVDA in some modes) alongside the restored role="columnheader"/headers association, not a regression, a known limitation of this label pattern. Added to README.md under "Known limitations", noting role="region" (2.0.7) at least keeps the table clearly bounded even where this happens.

Added an opt-in "Load only on com_content pages" setting (default off, matching prior versions exactly): the plugin's ~10KB CSS/JS normally loads on every frontend page regardless of whether that page has a table at all, since onBeforeCompileHead fires before Joomla knows what's in body. When enabled, onBeforeCompileHead() checks option=com_content early and returns before touching the Web Asset Manager at all on any other page, a real, measurable saving on a content-heavy site. Off by default because a table this plugin should style can legitimately live outside com_content too (a module, another component's output), and the setting's description warns about that trade-off explicitly.

Reverted 2.0.14's font-size: 0.9375rem back to font-size: 15px on table.responsiv, confirmed as a real regression on the actual production site (mechanizmysevcik.sk/cennik): rem is relative to the html root element's font-size, and this site's template (T3 Framework / Bootstrap 3, theme3556) evidently resets that root size to something well below the usual 16px default, a very common pattern in older Bootstrap 3 templates. The result was noticeably smaller table text than before, not the intended "same size at default, scales with user preference" outcome.

The WCAG 1.4.4 motivation for 2.0.14 wasn't wrong in principle, but a relative unit is only actually more accessible if it reliably resolves to a sensible size, here it silently produced a worse, smaller result on a real site than the plain pixel value it replaced. A fixed 15px still respects a user's browser zoom (which scales pixel values too in every modern browser); reverting to it is the safer, predictable choice given the direct evidence of breakage, rather than defending a partial accessibility gain that made real reading harder.

Verified via headless render: with the page's root font-size forced to 20px (the same test used to confirm 2.0.14's scaling), the table's computed font-size is now 15px regardless, matching the pre-2.0.14 behaviour exactly, on any host page irrespective of what it sets on html.

Added print styles: --rwd-card-shadow and the scroll-shadow indicators render as flat grey bands on paper (a screen-only affordance), so @media print now drops all box-shadows, lets .rwd-table-wrap show its full content instead of a clipped/scrollable overflow, and asks each stacked card's row not to split across a page break (break-inside: avoid) where the printer/browser honours it.

Added a @media (forced-colors: active) rule (Windows High Contrast and similar modes) setting border-color: CanvasText on the table and its cells, so the grid lines stay visible and consistent with surrounding forced-colors text instead of disappearing.

Verified the print rules via headless render with page.emulateMediaType('print'): a card's box-shadow goes from the normal rgba(0,0,0,0.08) 0 1px 3px to none, the wrap's overflow-x goes from auto to visible, and break-inside: avoid applies, all only in print, screen rendering unaffected. The forced-colors rule could not be verified the same way (the headless Chrome build available in this environment doesn't support emulating that media feature), CSS syntax is unambiguous and the file parses/loads correctly, but this specific rule should get a real screen-reader/high-contrast pass before being treated as fully confirmed.

Fixed a WCAG 1.4.4 accessibility issue from the same external analysis: table.responsiv { font-size: 15px } used an absolute pixel value, overriding the user's browser base font-size setting instead of scaling with it. Changed to 0.9375rem (equal to 15px only at the default 16px root size, but now genuinely scales). legacy.css's 1.15rem was already rem-based and needed no change.

Fixed a manifest hygiene issue: none of the plugin's seven radio fields nor its one list field (card_style) had validate="options", the core convention (e.g. plg_system_httpheaders) that stops an out-of-range value from ever being saved. card_style also had no filter at all; added filter="cmd".

Verified via headless render: with the page's root font-size set to 20px, the table's computed font-size is 18.75px (0.9375 × 20), confirming it now scales; at the default 16px root it still renders as the original 15px, so no visible change for the common case.

Corrected a factual mistake from the original CSS comment, caught by the same external analysis and confirmed against the actual Joomla source: data-color-scheme is NOT something Cassiopeia (Joomla 5's default frontend template) sets, that attribute belongs to Atum, the ADMINISTRATOR template. Cassiopeia has no built-in dark-mode switch at all (a third-party plugin, "Dark Magic", exists specifically to add one, because Cassiopeia doesn't). Since this plugin only ever runs on the frontend (isClient('site')), the old :root[data-color-scheme="dark"] rule realistically matched almost nowhere in practice.

What real commercial/frontend templates commonly use instead is Bootstrap 5.3's own data-bs-theme="dark", and typically not on html at all, but on body or some other wrapper. Rewrote the dark-mode trigger as a plain, unscoped [data-color-scheme="dark"], [data-bs-theme="dark"] attribute selector (matches on any ancestor, not just :root, the resulting custom-property values still inherit down correctly regardless of which ancestor carries the attribute) plus the same prefers-color-scheme OS-level fallback as before.
Added color-scheme: light dark; on .rwd-table-wrap so its own scrollbar (when the table genuinely scrolls) matches whichever mode is active instead of always rendering light.

Verified via headless render: data-bs-theme="dark" on body (the realistic case, previously not covered at all) now correctly applies the dark palette; data-color-scheme="dark" on html (Atum-style, in case some other custom setup mirrors it) still works as before; plain light mode with neither attribute is unaffected.

Fixed a P2 finding from the same external analysis: wrapCellValues() ran unconditionally for every enhanced table, wrapping every td[data-label]'s content in span class="rwd-value" regardless of whether that table would ever actually stack into cards, and regardless of the "Fill data-label" setting. Confirmed the risk was real, not theoretical: this mutation can break a template's or third-party script's own selectors (td > a, td > img:first-child, td:empty) and changes childNodes for anyone else reading the cell, including on tables that live comfortably at desktop width and never stack at all.

wrapCellValues() now only runs lazily, from inside observeWidth()'s apply(), on a pass where the table is actually about to be (or already is) .is-stacked, a table that never crosses the breakpoint never has its cells touched. wrapCellValues() was already idempotent per cell (data-rwd-wrapped guard), so calling it on every already-stacked pass afterwards remains a safe no-op.

Verified via headless render: a table in a 900px wrapper (never stacks) ends with zero span.rwd-value elements and its a cell content remains a direct child of td (td > a still matches); a table in a 300px wrapper (stacks) is wrapped as before; and a table that starts wide and is then resized narrow gets wrapped at exactly the point it crosses the breakpoint, not before. All prior fixes (2.0.2,2.0.11) re-verified unaffected by this change.

Fixed a P2 finding from the same external analysis: ensureWrap() assumed table.parentElement was never null and called parent.insertBefore(...) unconditionally, a detached table (built in memory by another script, or momentarily disconnected during a DOM move) would throw a TypeError there and abort the whole forEach in enhance(), leaving every table after it in that pass unprocessed.
ensureWrap() now returns the table itself when it has no parent, instead of throwing.

Honest note on reachability: collectTables() only ever finds tables via document.querySelectorAll(), which by definition only returns elements currently connected to the document, so within the plugin's own code as written today, a table reaching ensureWrap() with parentElement === null in the same synchronous pass doesn't appear to occur. The guard is still worth having: it's a one-line, zero-downside protection against API misuse or a future refactor (e.g. a MutationObserver path that processes addedNodes directly instead of re-querying the document) reintroducing exactly this crash.

Verified against the real, exported enhance() (via window.rwdTablesEnhance()), not a reimplementation: document.querySelectorAll was temporarily wrapped to also return a genuinely detached table class="responsiv" (created but never appended anywhere) alongside the page's real table. The call completed without throwing, the detached table was processed without error (no wrap, since there's nowhere to put one), and, the actual point of the fix, the real table on the page was still fully processed (data-rwd-ready, wrapped) rather than the whole pass aborting on the bad one.

Fixed a P2 finding from the same external analysis: observeWidth()'s ResizeObserver (and the window.addEventListener("resize", apply) fallback for browsers without it) never disconnected/removed themselves, on a page that dynamically swaps tables in and out (an editor, an AJAX-refreshed panel, notably more likely now that 2.0.9 added opt-in DOM watching), that's a growing memory leak and pointless callback work for elements no longer on the page.

apply() now checks target.isConnected on each run and tears itself down at that point (ro.disconnect() for the ResizeObserver path, window.removeEventListener for the fallback), opportunistic rather than instant (neither mechanism itself reports removal), but correct, and simpler than adding a second observer just to watch for removals in what should be a rare case. WeakRef was considered and left out: the actual retention is ResizeObserver's own internal tracking and the window-level listener closure, not something a WeakRef on our side would change, disconnecting explicitly is the real fix.

Verified via headless render on the fallback path (forced by deleting window.ResizeObserver before the script loads, since it's the deterministically testable one, the ResizeObserver fires only on genuine size changes, not on disconnection alone, so it can't be triggered on demand the same way): removeEventListener('resize', ...) fires exactly once after the table is removed and a resize occurs, and a further resize afterwards produces no additional add/remove calls, confirming the listener is genuinely gone rather than silently re-added.

Added an opt-in "Watch for dynamically added tables" setting (default off), addressing a real gap the same external analysis pointed out: enhance() only ever ran once (DOMContentLoaded) plus whenever a page explicitly calls window.rwdTablesEnhance(), a table injected later by AJAX (a lazy-loaded tab/accordion panel, SP Page Builder, a custom fetch) stayed unprocessed unless whoever built that integration happened to know about the manual escape hatch.

This is a genuine trade-off, not a plain bug fix: an always-on MutationObserver watching the whole page would be exactly the kind of standing cost a system plugin running on every request shouldn't impose by default, which is what an earlier review pass in this same project explicitly (and correctly) argued against. Making it an opt-in setting, off by default, resolves that tension, sites that need it can turn it on, sites that don't pay nothing extra.

When enabled, a MutationObserver on document.body looks for added table elements (or any added node containing one) and re-runs enhance() via requestIdleCallback (or setTimeout where unsupported), safe to call repeatedly since data-rwd-ready already makes it a no-op for tables already processed.

Verified via headless render: with the setting off, a table injected 100ms after page load stays unprocessed (matches prior behaviour exactly); with it on, the same injected table is automatically enhanced (data-rwd-ready="1", wrapped) with no manual call needed.

Fixed a P2 finding from the same external analysis: ensureWrap() recycled an existing .table-wrapper div unconditionally, a template that wraps a whole block of content in one .table-wrapper containing two (or more) tables meant both tables shared a single wrap. Confirmed: two tables in one .table-wrapper measured tables: 2 on the same element. Consequences: observeWidth() ran twice on that one element (two ResizeObservers, two scroll listeners on the same node), .is-stacked was driven by the shared wrapper's width rather than either table's own situation, and a .no-responsiv table inside it would still get the shared wrap's classes.

ensureWrap() now only reuses an existing .table-wrapper when it contains exactly one table; otherwise the table gets its own .rwd-table-wrap nested inside it, same as any table with no pre-existing wrapper.
Added a data-rwd-observed guard in observeWidth() so the same target element can never end up with a second ResizeObserver/scroll listener, as defense in depth beyond the ensureWrap() fix.

Verified via headless render: two tables in one shared .table-wrapper now each get their own independent wrap (data-rwd-observed="1" on both, confirmed as two distinct elements) and the shared wrapper itself is left untouched (no rwd-table-wrap class); a single table in a .table-wrapper still recycles it exactly as before (no regression).

Addressed another P2 finding from the same external analysis: the scrollable wrap gained tabindex="0" (since 1.2.0/2.0.6) but no role="region" and no accessible name, a screen reader would announce the Tab stop with nothing to identify it by. Added role="region" plus aria-label, sourced from the table's own caption when present, otherwise a translated fallback string.

Non-trivial architecture note the analysis caught: plugin language files install under administrator/language regardless of client (Joomla's PluginAdapter/Installer::parseLanguages() always uses client id 1 for plugins), and $autoloadLanguage was removed in 2.0.0 as apparently-unused, so the frontend had no plugin strings loaded at all. Fixed by calling $this->loadLanguage() explicitly in onBeforeCompileHead() before resolving Text::_('PLG_SYSTEM_FGRESPONSIVETABLES_SCROLL_REGION'), then handing that string to JS via addScriptOptions (scrollLabel), Text::_() alone on the frontend would have silently returned the raw, untranslated key.

Verified via headless render across three cases: a scrollable table with a caption (label taken from the caption, ignoring scrollLabel), a scrollable table with no caption (label falls back to the translated scrollLabel), and a table that isn't scrollable at all (no tabindex, no role, no aria-label, confirms the "only when needed" behavior from 1.9.5/2.0.x still holds).

Addressed a P2 finding from the same external analysis: the horizontal-scroll shadow/keyboard-focus feature (1.2.0/1.2 era) was effectively dead code in practice. table.responsiv { width: 100% } with table-layout:auto and no min-width means a browser will shrink columns to fit rather than overflow, so in the width band between the stacking breakpoint (default 600px) and "plenty of room", a tablet, a narrow module, an open accordion, a wide table neither stacks into cards nor scrolls; it just squeezes into unreadable multi-line column headers, and scrollWidth never exceeds clientWidth so the scroll cue and tabindex never activate. Confirmed: a 700px wrapper with five long headers measured clientWidth === scrollWidth === 700.

Added a new setting, "Minimum table width (px)" (default 0 = off, matching prior behaviour exactly). When set, JS sets a --rwd-min-width custom property (inline style) on the table's wrap, and CSS applies it as min-width on the non-stacked table, giving the browser a genuine reason to overflow instead of shrink, which is what the existing scroll-shadow/tabindex logic actually needs to have anything to react to.

Verified via headless render, same scenario both with the setting off and on: off is byte-for-byte the old behaviour (scrollWidth === clientWidth, no tabindex, no scroll shadow); on with e.g. 900px measures scrollWidth 900 vs. clientWidth 700, tabindex="0" is added, and can-scroll-right activates, the existing (already well-written) scroll indicator now has a real signal to respond to.

Fixed the fourth real bug from the same external analysis, and the sharpest one: applyLabels() tracked column position with a fresh colIndex per row, so a td rowspan="2" in one body row silently shifted every later cell in the FOLLOWING row one column to the left (nothing there to advance past). Confirmed before the fix: trtd rowspan="2"Pondelok/tdtdAD08/tdtd60 €/td/trtrtdAD20/tdtd70 €/td/tr labelled the second row's cells "Deň"/"Stroj" instead of "Stroj"/"Cena", a real price shown under the wrong column name on mobile, not just misalignment.

applyLabels() now tracks an occupied grid across rows ("row:col" -> true), the same approach headerLabels() already used for header rows with rowspan/colspan, a rowspan cell reserves its column in the following row(s), so the next row's real cells correctly advance past it instead of shifting into its place.

Verified via headless render on the exact reported scenario: the second row's cells now report data-label="Stroj" and data-label="Cena" (previously "Deň"/"Stroj"). All fixes from 2.0.2,2.0.4 re-verified unaffected (colspan/rowspan header resolution, tbody th row-header, no-thead fallback header row).

Fixed a third real bug from the same external analysis: a table with no real thead, the common TinyMCE output where the author types trth.../th/tr as the first row directly inside tbody, had its header row correctly read by headerLabels()'s existing fallback, but nothing hid that row visually in stacked mode, so it rendered as its own near-empty card of bare th cells side by side. A quieter second bug in the same case: applyAriaRoles() decided "is this a header cell" purely from row.parentElement === table.tHead, so those th cells got role="rowheader"/scope="row" (a row header) instead of the column-header role they actually are, wrong structure for screen reader users.

Added markHeaderRow(): when a table has no table.tHead and its first row's cells are all th, tags that row with class rwd-headrow. CSS hides it the same visually-hidden way as a real thead, and applyAriaRoles()'s inHead check now also recognizes it, so those cells get role="columnheader"/scope="col" correctly. Runs unconditionally (not gated behind the "Fill data-label" setting), since the visual-hiding half of the fix matters regardless of that setting.

Verified via headless render: the marked row is visually hidden (position:absolute + zero-size clip, same as thead), its th cells report role="columnheader"/scope="col", data-label on the following data row is unaffected, and the card list shows exactly one card per data row with no extra near-empty header card. Fixes from 2.0.2 and 2.0.3 re-verified unaffected.

Fixed another real bug from the same external analysis: a th scope="row" used as the first cell of a body row (a common accessible "row header" pattern, instead of a plain td) was never switched out of display: table-cell for the stacked layout, it rendered as a narrow strip taking only its own content width inside a now-block tr, with empty space beside it, instead of spanning the card like every other line. Confirmed via computed style (display: table-cell, ~60px wide) and screenshot before the fix.
tbody th / tfoot th now get display: block, styled as the card's header line (reusing --rwd-head, matching the visually-hidden thead's own header color).

First attempt at the fix used width: 100% alongside padding, which overflowed the card by ~19px (no box-sizing: border-box is set anywhere in this stylesheet), removed the redundant width: 100% instead, since a block-level element already fills its container's width correctly on its own; a border-box reset for the whole plugin was considered but not applied, to avoid touching unrelated layout that has never needed it.

Verified via headless render: display is now block, width matches the card (322px vs. 324px card width, the 2px being the card's own border), and the row-header line visually spans the full card as its header, both before/after screenshots compared. Existing long-value-wrap and rwd-nowrap behavior from 2.0.2 unaffected.

Fixed a real card-overflow bug found by an external analysis (Perplexity): the mobile card's value column used white-space: nowrap with a plain auto grid track, so a long text value (a note, a description, not just a short price) forced the whole card wider than its wrap and overflowed sideways with no visual cue (the scroll-shadow indicator and keyboard focus are both intentionally suppressed while .is-stacked, since a stacked card shouldn't normally need to scroll at all). Measured at 360px viewport before the fix: wrap clientWidth 344px vs. scrollWidth 834px.

Value now wraps by default (white-space: normal; overflow-wrap: anywhere;), and both grid columns use minmax(0, ...) so the tracks can actually shrink below their content's natural width, the earlier plain 1fr auto looked fine for short values only because grid's default track minimum is content-based, not because the layout was actually safe. Added an opt-in rwd-nowrap class for a td whose value is always short and should never wrap regardless of the label next to it.

Verified via headless-browser render: the reported scenario now measures scrollWidth === clientWidth (344px), long values wrap and stay inside the card, short values are unaffected, and rwd-nowrap still forces a single line when explicitly requested.
Desktop table header font-size increased from 0.85em to 0.95em, was noticeably small.

Rebranded into the FG series as plg_system_fgresponsivetables (element, namespace FG\Plugin\System\Fgresponsivetables, language files, media destination, display name all renamed accordingly). Version numbering restarted at 2.0.0; the pre-rebrand history (originally built for mechanizmysevcik.sk and fnspza.sk, 1.0.0,1.9.7) is preserved in the project's earlier development notes, not repeated here.

Functionally identical to 1.9.7 at the point of rebrand: stacks table.responsiv into labelled, accessible cards on narrow screens (CSS Grid label/value layout, ARIA roles compensating for display:block, colspan/rowspan-aware header resolution, nested-table-safe DOM traversal), with admin-configurable breakpoint, card style, optional float-clearing, and an opt-in legacy.css for the original sites' generically-named helper classes (.day-content, .sirka-*, etc.).
Removed protected $autoloadLanguage = true; (unused on the frontend side; kept out going forward per FG convention).
Added an extension update server (updates.xml on the repo's master branch, clientsite/client declared for the plugin entry).
